metadata.title: Old-Population Hypervelocity Stars from the Galactic Center: Limits from the SDSS

evidence.quote:
We select candidate unbound ejected stars with exactly the criterion as bound stars
(eq. [1]), except reversing the sign on the second condition,v _ { \odot - \mathrm { c i r c l e } } \ \geq \ v _ { \mathrm { e s c } }, and of course
demanding that they be exiting rather than entering the Galaxy.

There is one F star candidate that survives our selection criteria and one G star. The
proper motions for both of these stars are inconsistent with a Galactocentric origin as we
now show.

We additionally find 2 candidate unbound stars (one F
and one G), however, existing proper motion measurements make these unlikely
to be emerging from the GC.

notes: SDSSJ111107.85+585357.2 (F, V_G=+425.4) and SDSSJ224740.09-004451.6 (G, V_G=+401.8) are the two positive-velocity entries selected as candidate unbound ejectees by the reversed criterion in T:p8-b1 and reported in T:p8-b4; T:p1-b3 calls them “2 candidate unbound stars.” T:p8-b6 and T:p8-b7 find proper motions inconsistent with a Galactocentric origin and call a GC unbound-ejectee interpretation unlikely, but the paper still labels them candidate unbound stars and Table 1 candidate ejectees (T:p12-b0), so I retain them with that caveat. The four negative-velocity F rows in T:p12-b0—SDSSJ061118.63+642618.5, SDSSJ074557.31+181246.7, SDSSJ224052.56+011332.1, and SDSSJ211321.02+103456.7—are described as candidate bound ejectees in T:p4-b6 and are excluded because they are not present-day Galactic-unbound candidates.

SDSSJ111107.85+585357.2: The target SDSSJ111107.85+585357.2 is the positive-velocity F star in Table 1 and is identified in §3.5 as the unbound F-star candidate. Its Table 1 V_G=+425.4±3.1 km/s is a Galactocentric radial velocity, not a heliocentric/barycentric RV, so the Galactocentric frame is stated explicitly. The paper gives this candidate's proper motion as a magnitude and position angle (34 mas/yr at 55°), not as equatorial RA/Dec components; converting to components would require an unsupported calculation. No individual distance, parallax, galactocentric radius, total Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this target. The 7.8 kpc distance estimate in §3.5 applies to the G-star candidate, not this F-star target.

SDSSJ224740.09-004451.6: The target is the single G-star candidate in Table 1, SDSSJ224740.09-004451.6. Its only listed velocity is V_G = +401.8 ± 13.1 km/s (T:p12-b0), described as a Galactocentric radial velocity; it is not extracted as radial_velocity because the rules limit that quantity to heliocentric or barycentric line-of-sight velocities and exclude velocities relative to the local/Galactic standard of rest. The proper motion is reported only as a total magnitude and Galactic position angle (6 mas/yr at 183°; T:p8-b7), not as equatorial proper-motion components, so it is not extracted as proper_motion_ra or proper_motion_dec.
